source.authors: Andrés Taucare‐Ríos, Dyana Leiva, Jheremy Mendez-Yovera, Claudio Reyes-Olivares
source.title: Thermal ecology of the South American leaf-toed gecko Phyllodactylus gerrhopygus (Wiegmann, 1834) (Gekkota, Phyllodactylidae) in northern Chile

method: behavioural thermal-gradient choice in the laboratory: body temperature of free-moving geckos read every 5 min for 1 h in a 10 to 40 C horizontal gradient, once in the morning and once in the evening
conditions: Wild geckos collected by hand under rocks and debris at the Huayquique Campus near Huayquique Beach, Iquique, northern Chile, spring 2023; 20 individuals (9 adults, 11 juveniles, juvenile = SVL <= 50 mm); sex composition not reported. Kept about two weeks in the laboratory (25.5 +/- 2.5 C, 62 +/- 3.1 % RH, 12L:12D with natural light; week one acclimation, week two testing), fed live Loxosceles laeta ad libitum and fasted 3 days before trials. Horizontal gradient 10 to 40 C in a glass container (0.5 x 0.1 x 0.1 m) half-submerged in water in a thermoregulated chamber, 100 W titanium heater at one end, cooling gels at the other, infrared lamps above, thin sand floor with refuges; 1 h acclimation in the gradient, then readings every 5 min for 1 h; morning trials 10:30 to 11:30 h and evening trials 19:30 to 20:30 h. Each animal appears to have been tested in both periods but the order and interval between the two trials are not stated. Values are means +/- SD as printed; the Results repeat them. Time of day effect F1,17 = 18.36, p = 0.0005 (the df do not obviously match 20 animals; reported as printed); age class had no effect (F1,17 = 0.14, p = 0.71; juveniles 28.83 +/- 7.80 C, adults 28.23 +/- 4.52 C, overall 28.63 +/- 9.41 C, Table 1); Tpref did not differ from body temperature (t18 = 1.45, p = 0.15) or substrate temperature (t18 = 1.5, p = 0.14) and was not related to SVL (p = 0.16) or mass (p = 0.15), but was related to air temperature (t18 = 2.36, p = 0.02). No exclusions mentioned. Behavioural choice of a free-moving animal, not a receptor threshold.
quote: The Tpref was significantly higher during the evening (32.23 ± 5.91 °C) than the morning period (25.2 ± 9.02 °C).
note: Sentence read whole in one piece from the Herpetozoa page (Abstract). Evening and morning values are two lines from one sentence. Family from the paper (Gekkota, Phyllodactylidae) and Reptile Database (Phyllodactylidae, Squamata, Wiegmann 1834; the paper names no order). source.authors: Vaishnavi Apte, Avichal Tatu, Maria Thaker
source.title: Microhabitat level thermal physiology and thermoregulation of a diurnal gecko in an urban landscape
source.journal: Frontiers in Amphibian and Reptile Science 2: 1522805

method: behavioural thermal-gradient choice in the laboratory: head surface temperature read every 5 min for 1 h in a 12 to 40 C gradient; Tset = median per lizard
conditions: Wild adults (SVL >= 2.4 cm; visibly gravid females excluded) hand-caught in urban Bengaluru, India, on two microhabitat types (19 on trees, 21 on walls; Table 1 sex split 10 male and 9 female on trees, 12 male and 9 female on walls), five locations, December to April; held individually 24 h at 26 to 28 C with water and 4 to 5 Drosophila daily, released at capture sites within two days. Thermal gradient 55 x 22 x 18 cm (aluminium base, acrylic walls) spanning 12 to 40 C with a heating pad at one end and ice packs at the other; each lizard started at the centre, acclimated 10 min, then head surface temperature was read by infrared gun every 5 min for 1 h (surface temperature strongly correlated with cloacal temperature, Supplementary Material 1); trials ran 0900 to 2000 h; each lizard's Tset is the median of its readings and the value is the mean of those Tset values (SE as printed). The same 40 lizards were used for CTmin then CTmax (3 h recovery); whether Tset was run before or after these tests is not stated. Microhabitat did not predict Tset (t = -0.32, p = 0.75, model with sex and SVL). Behavioural choice of a free-moving animal, not a receptor threshold.
quote: Tset estimates ranged from 24.4°C to 27.7°C (mean = 26.26 ± 0.57°C S.E.; N = 40) across all individuals from both the microhabitat types.
